chunks: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Indeed, God cannot be described. And how can He be described, when He has already said in His Book:
"And they do not appreciate God with the appreciation that is due to Him" [Quran 6:91]
Thus, He cannot be described with any estimation except that He would be greater than that.'

key_terms.أَعْظَمَ: greater, mightier — God always surpasses whatever estimation or description is imposed upon Him
key_terms.حَقَّ قَدْرِهِ: the appreciation truly due to Him — Quranic phrase asserting the utter inadequacy of human cognition before God
key_terms.قَدَرٍ: estimation, measure — any humanly conceived standard applied to God
key_terms.يُوصَفُ: is described — human attempts to circumscribe divine attributes in language

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq (AS) teach in al-Kafi about the prohibition of describing God beyond His own self-disclosure?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) asserts the absolute transcendence of God beyond all human description, grounding his teaching in Quran 6:91 as divine testimony. The argument is self-reinforcing: since God Himself declared that humans cannot appreciate Him as He deserves, any measure or characterisation applied to Him automatically falls short — God is always vaster than whatever is ascribed to Him.
